details:
Allah says: (The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed of grain which grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies His reward for whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing) Surah Al-Baqarah (261).

Allah says: (If you loan Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative and Forbearing) Surah At-Taghabun (17).
earnings: 700 hasanat for every pound spent

details: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Whoever kills a gecko with the first strike, one hundred hasanat are written for him; with the second strike, less than that; with the third, less than that). In another narration from Abu Hurairah, the Prophet ﷺ said: (seventy hasanat for the first strike). Narrated by Muslim.
earnings: 100 hasanat

details: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (I saw a man strolling in Paradise because of a tree he cut from the road that used to harm people). Narrated by Muslim.
earnings: Strolling in Paradise
time: An hour or less (depending on the situation)

details: Al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (No two Muslims meet and shake hands except that they are forgiven before they part). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud; see Sahih Sunan Abi Dawud by Al-Albani no. 5212.
earnings: Forgiveness before parting

details: Humran, the freed slave of Uthman, reported that he saw Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) call for water, pour it over his hands three times and wash them, then put his right hand in the vessel, rinse his mouth and nose, wash his face three times, wash his arms to the elbows three times, wipe his head, then wash his feet three times to the ankles, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine and then prays two rak'ahs without letting his thoughts wander, his past sins are forgiven). In another narration: (except that he is forgiven for what is between it and the next prayer). Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
earnings: Forgiveness of past sins

details: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Do you think that if there were a river at the door of one of you and he bathed in it five times a day, any dirt would remain on him? They said: No dirt would remain. He said: That is the example of the five daily prayers; Allah erases sins through them). Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
earnings: Erasure of sins

details: Asma bint Yazid (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever defends the flesh of his brother against backbiting, it becomes due upon Allah to free him from the Fire). In another narration: (Whoever defends his brother, Allah turns the punishment of the Fire away from him on the Day of Resurrection). And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: (And it was due upon Us to support the believers). Reported by Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, Ahmad and At-Tabarani; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' no. 6240.
earnings: Freedom from the Fire
time: A minute or a few minutes

details: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Whoever fasts a day for the sake of Allah, Allah keeps his face away from the Fire by seventy autumns). Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
earnings: Keeping the Fire seventy years away from your face

details:
Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever prays to Allah for forty days in congregation, catching the first takbir, two exonerations are written for him: exoneration from the Fire and exoneration from hypocrisy). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi; graded hasan by Al-Albani in Sahih At-Tirmidhi no. 241.

Allah says: (So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained success. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion) Al-Imran 185.
earnings: Exoneration from the Fire and from hypocrisy
mission: Praying in congregation and catching the opening takbir
time: A few minutes before the iqamah

details: Abu Dharr and Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, even the size of a sandgrouse's nest, Allah builds for him a house in Paradise). Narrated by Ibn Majah; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' no. 6128. (A sandgrouse's nest: the nest of the qata bird.)
earnings: A house in Paradise

details: Umm Habibah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever prays twelve rak'ahs in a day and night, a house is built for him in Paradise: four before Dhuhr, two after it, two after Maghrib, two after Isha, and two before Fajr). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi; authenticated by Al-Albani.
earnings: A house in Paradise

details:
Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (In Paradise there are chambers whose outside can be seen from their inside and whose inside can be seen from their outside. It was asked: For whom are they, O Messenger of Allah? He said: For those who speak kindly, feed others, pray at night while people sleep). Narrated by Ahmad and Al-Bayhaqi; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih at-Targhib no. 946.

Allah says: (And those who believe and do righteous deeds — We will surely settle them in chambers of Paradise beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Excellent is the reward of the workers) (58) Surah Al-Ankabut.
earnings: Chambers in Paradise

details:
Abu Rafi' (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever washes a Muslim and conceals it is forgiven forty times; whoever digs his grave and buries him receives reward like the reward of housing him until the Day of Resurrection; whoever shrouds him, Allah clothes him on the Day of Resurrection with the silk and brocade of Paradise). Narrated by Al-Hakim, Al-Bayhaqi and At-Tabarani; graded hasan by Al-Albani.

Allah says: (Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and brocade. And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a purifying drink) Surah Al-Insan (21).
earnings: Forgiveness forty times + clothing of Paradise silk

details:
Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever swallows his anger while able to act upon it, Allah calls him before all creation and lets him choose from the wide-eyed houris to marry whomever he wishes). Narrated by Abu Dawud and At-Tirmidhi; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Sunan At-Tirmidhi no. 2021.

Allah says: (Thus. And We will marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes) Surah Ad-Dukhan (54).
earnings: Marriage to the houris of Paradise

details: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever performs ablution well, then looks up to the sky and says: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger — the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him to enter from whichever he wishes). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi and Ahmad; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' no. 55.
earnings: Eight gates of Paradise opened — enter from whichever you choose
mission: Ablution and the remembrance after it
time: Ablution plus the remembrance after it

details: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever prays the morning prayer in congregation, then sits remembering Allah until the sun rises, then prays two rak'ahs, receives the reward of a Hajj and an Umrah. He said: complete, complete, complete). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Sunan Abi Dawud no. 6346.
earnings: Reward of a complete Hajj and Umrah
mission: Fajr prayer and sitting until sunrise
time: About an hour and a half

details:
Abu Umamah al-Bahili (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever walks to an obligatory congregational prayer, it is like a Hajj; whoever walks to a voluntary prayer, it is like an Umrah). Narrated by At-Tabarani; graded hasan by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' no. 6556.

Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Whoever performs ablution for prayer, perfects it, then walks to the obligatory prayer and prays it with the people or in congregation or in the mosque — his sins are forgiven). Narrated by Muslim.

Allah says: (Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds — indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds) Surah Al-Kahf (30).
earnings: Reward of Hajj, or forgiveness of sins

details:
Aws ibn Aws ath-Thaqafi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Whoever washes on Friday, takes a bath, goes early and arrives early, walks and does not ride, sits close to the imam, listens and does not engage in idle talk — for every step he takes there is the reward of a year: its fasting and its night prayers). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah 898.

Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Whoever bathes on Friday the bath of janabah, then goes early — it is as if he sacrificed a camel; whoever goes in the second hour, as if he sacrificed a cow; in the third hour, as if he sacrificed a horned ram; in the fourth, as if he sacrificed a chicken; in the fifth, as if he sacrificed an egg. When the imam comes out, the angels attend to listen to the remembrance). Agreed upon.

Ibn Uthaymeen said: It begins at sunrise — and it was said from dawn, but the first is more correct, because the time before sunrise is the time of Fajr prayer. End of quote. Majmu' Fatawa of Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen (16 / question 1260).
earnings: For every step, the reward of a year of fasting and praying

details: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Whoever performs tawaf around the House and prays two rak'ahs is like one who frees a slave). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' no. 6379.
earnings: Reward of freeing a slave

details: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever loves that his provision be extended and his lifespan lengthened, let him maintain his family ties). Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
earnings: Extended provision and good remembrance

details: Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (The believer reaches by his good character the rank of the one who fasts and prays at night). Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud no. 4798.
earnings: Reaching the rank of the fasting, praying person
time: All the time — no specific time needed

details: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The most beloved of you to me and the nearest of you to me in seating on the Day of Resurrection are the best of you in manners. The most hateful of you to me and the farthest from me in seating on the Day of Resurrection are the chatterers, the pompous, and the arrogant). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih At-Tirmidhi no. 2018.
earnings: The Prophet's love and nearness to him ﷺ on the Day of Resurrection

details: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (No Muslim visits a sick Muslim in the morning except that seventy thousand angels pray for him until the evening; if he visits in the evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him until the morning; and he will have a harvest in Paradise). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' no. 5767.
earnings: Seventy thousand angels pray for you

details: Zaid ibn Khalid al-Juhani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Whoever feeds a fasting person, the same reward as his is written for him, without diminishing the fasting person's reward at all; whoever equips a warrior in the way of Allah or takes care of his family in his absence, the same reward as his is written for him, without diminishing the warrior's reward at all). Narrated by Ahmad and At-Tirmidhi; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' no. 6414.
earnings: The same reward as the fasting person or the warrior (100% profit)
mission: Feeding a fasting person and equipping a warrior

details: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Whoever relieves a believer of a worldly hardship, Allah relieves him of a hardship of the Day of Resurrection; whoever eases the burden of one in difficulty, Allah eases for him in this world and the next; whoever conceals a Muslim, Allah conceals him in this world and the next; and Allah is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother...). Narrated by Muslim.
earnings: Relief on the Day of Resurrection, ease, and Allah's concealment in this world and the next

details: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Whoever prays over a funeral and does not follow it receives a qirat; if he follows it, he receives two qirats. It was asked: What are the two qirats? He said: The smaller of them is like Mount Uhud). Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
earnings: One or two qirats

details: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Allah says: Where are those who loved one another for My glory? Today I shade them in My shade, a day when there is no shade but Mine). Narrated by Muslim.
earnings: Shade under Allah's Throne

details:
Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Allah and His angels, even the ant in its hole and the whale in the sea, send blessings upon the one who teaches people goodness). Narrated by At-Tabarani; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' no. 1838.

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ asking for a mount, but he found nothing to give him, so he directed him to another who gave him one. The man told the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: (The one who guides to goodness is like its doer). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi; authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih At-Tirmidhi no. 2670.
earnings: Supplication from Allah, the angels, the ant and the whale — for as long as you teach

details: Jarir ibn Abdullah said: Some Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wearing wool; he saw their bad state and need, so he urged people to give charity, but they were slow until it showed on his face. Then a man from the Ansar came with a pouch of silver, then another came, and they followed one after another until joy was visible on his face. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam and it is followed after him, the same reward as those who follow it is written for him, without diminishing their rewards at all; whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam and it is followed after him, the same burden as those who follow it is written upon him, without diminishing their burdens at all). Narrated by Muslim.
earnings: The reward of everyone who follows it, until the Day of Resurrection

details: Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Every morning, charity is due on every joint of each of you: every tasbihah is charity, every tahmidah is charity, every tahlilah is charity, every takbirah is charity, enjoining good is charity, forbidding evil is charity — and two rak'ahs prayed in the forenoon suffice for all of that). Narrated by Muslim; Al-Bukhari narrated part of it.
earnings: Charity on behalf of every joint of the bones

details: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted the entire year). Narrated by Muslim.
earnings: Reward of fasting an entire year

details: Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will have mercy upon you. The womb is derived from the Most Merciful: whoever maintains it, Allah maintains him; whoever severs it, Allah severs him). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi; authenticated by Al-Albani.
earnings: Mercy from Allah, the Most High

details: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Whoever stands in prayer on Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins are forgiven; whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins are forgiven). Agreed upon.
earnings: Forgiveness of past sins

details: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins are forgiven). Agreed upon.
earnings: Forgiveness of past sins

details:
Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with them) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Allah's pleasure is in the pleasure of the parents, and Allah's anger is in the anger of the parents). Narrated by At-Tirmidhi (1821); authenticated by Ibn Hibban and Al-Hakim; graded hasan by Al-Albani in As-Silsilah as-Sahihah (516).

Allah says: (And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age while with you, say not to them so much as 'uff,' and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word. And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small) Al-Isra (23, 24).
earnings: The pleasure of Allah, the Most High
